thread:
alex: quick idea after the failover sims: split the "lease" signal into two logical artifacts. 1) tiny authoritative digest used by the global controlplane for routing/ownership decisions. 2) verbose telemetry (per-tenant histos, trace IDs) streamed to TSDB. keep the semantics identical but different pipes.

jamie: sounds promising. the global controller queue keeps getting thrashed during tenant migrations because of metric cardinality. how tiny is "tiny"?

alex: digest = {owner, seq, expiry_ts, region_hint, version} ~ <200 bytes. stored in a compact k/v index sharded by tenant. control reads only that. verbose stuff is async.

hana: operational concerns: if we introduce a sidecar that publishes digests, what's the failure mode if the sidecar dies? we can't afford false owner flips.
mikael: keep a fallback: region-agent continues to hold the authoritative local heartbeat and can advertise a degraded-digest if sidecar offline. sidecar is an optimization for cardinality and export rates, not the source of truth.

jamie: won't this force another global migration to add the k/v index? we should avoid big DB schema work. can we implement the index as an append-only partitioned store first?
alex: proposal: add a lightweight persistent store (new table) but with a migration plan: write-through from old controlplane for 30d and read-prefer new index in canary regions. no instant cutover.
hana: agree on gradual migration. also let's include a checksum or short HMAC in the digest so the controlplane can detect stale/mangled digests.
mikael: +1. use a 64-bit truncated HMAC with a known key ring so verifying is cheap. if mismatch, controller falls back to RPC to the region-agent for authoritative state.
jamie: what about time sync? TTL semantics are critical for failover windows. we saw clock skew cause unnecessary reclaims before.
alex: set TTL = 3x heartbeat_interval + jitter_buffer (2s) and require monotonic seq numbers from owners. controller only acts on digest if seq >= last_seen_seq. that prevents old digests from resurrecting owners.
hana: test plan: (A) sidecar crash during steady state, ensure no owner flip. (B) sidecar backfilled traces with high cardinality but controller unaffected. (C) simulated clock skew +-500ms. jamie can own (A) and (B), mikael takes (C).

mikael: also add a small audit-runner that randomly compares digest -> authoritative payload and logs diffs to S3 for 7d. helps postmortems without high QPS cost.
jamie: we should measure the expected reduction: rough estimate says controlplane metric cardinality drops 80-95% in synthetic workloads. that should bring queue latency back under SLO.

ops-bot: runbook note created: "lease-digest: if digest_verification fails, controller should query region-agent; mark tenant:digest: degraded and alert paging threshold if >5m"

alex: action items: 1) prototype sidecar that consumes existing heartbeat topic and writes digest to new k/v index (alex), 2) migration plan doc + schema (hana), 3) HMAC verifier library + unit tests (mikael), 4) chaos + canary tests (jamie). aim for a low-risk RFC and a single-region canary in two weeks.
hana: I'll draft migration steps and a non-blocking read-pref mechanism so we can flip per-region.
mikael: will stub verifier and tests this week. question: any objections to using sealed keys from KMS for the HMAC key?
jamie: KMS OK but store rotated keys and allow verifier to accept previous key for 24h to avoid race during roll.

alex: good call. I'll draft seq diagram and include the fallback RPC flow. sync tomorrow 10:30 for 30m?
hana: yes.
mikael: yes.
jamie: yes.
